items.detail: Goodwill plus tangible assets

items.label: 4. Sale agreement
items.detail: Assets and goodwill for shares plus DLA credit

items.label: 5. Trade and employees
items.detail: Transfer staff under TUPE

scenes.heading: The Process: Finishing Off
scenes.narration: Next, handle VAT either as a transfer of a going concern or a new registration, close the sole trader registrations, start the company compliance cycle, and elect to carry losses over under section 86.

scenes.heading: Critical Tax Mechanics
scenes.narration: Goodwill is usually a market value disposal, but section 162 incorporation relief defers the gain if the whole business goes in for shares. Watch stamp duty land tax on property, and the VAT going concern rules too.

items.label: CGT on goodwill
items.detail: s.162 defers if whole business goes for shares

items.label: SDLT on property
items.detail: Stamp duty land tax on any property moved

items.label: VAT TOGC
items.detail: No VAT charged if conditions are met

items.label: Director's loan account
items.detail: Credits the trader for net assets transferred

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll walk every step, weigh up the section 162 versus section 165 election, and work through the TUPE and employee considerations.

scenes.heading: Partnership to LLP or Limited Company
scenes.subheading: Two routes out of a partnership: one mostly painless, one a real transition
scenes.narration: Moving from a partnership to an LLP is mostly painless, because both are tax-transparent. Moving to a limited company is harder, as the business becomes a separate taxable entity.

scenes.heading: Partnership to LLP
scenes.narration: First, form the LLP so it mirrors the partnership's membership and profit-sharing ratio. HMRC's concession D33 then generally treats it as a continuation, so there's no cessation, no transfer pricing and no capital gains tax.

items.label: Form the LLP
items.detail: Mirror the partnership's membership

items.label: Match profit shares
items.detail: Keep the same profit-sharing ratio

items.label: Concession D33 applies
items.detail: Generally treated as a continuation

items.label: Business carries on
items.detail: Assets at carrying value, pools roll over

scenes.heading: LLP Route Versus Ltd Route
scenes.narration: The LLP route keeps continuity, and trading losses can be claimed by members on the same basis. The company route is treated like sole trader to limited company for each partner, with goodwill, capital gains and TUPE issues.

items.label: Partnership to LLP
items.detail: Continuation: no cessation, no CGT, pools roll over

items.label: Partnership to Ltd
items.detail: Real transition: goodwill, CGT and TUPE issues

scenes.heading: Key Issues Moving to a Ltd
scenes.narration: Each partner's share of goodwill triggers capital gains tax, though section 162 incorporation relief is available if the whole business goes in for shares. Losses can survive by election, and watch stamp duty land tax and VAT.

items.label: Goodwill and CGT
items.detail: Relief if whole business transferred for shares

items.label: Assets at market value
items.detail: Possible balancing charges

items.label: Trading losses
items.detail: Survive via election under CTA 2010

items.label: SDLT and VAT
items.detail: SDLT on property; VAT TOGC for the new Ltd

scenes.heading: Watch Profit-Sharing Changes
scenes.narration: This is critical: changing profit shares can trigger capital gains tax on goodwill, so structure carefully. And going from LLP to limited company uses the same mechanics, plus winding down the LLP at Companies House.

items.label: Profit-share changes
items.detail: Can trigger CGT on goodwill; structure carefully

items.label: LLP to Ltd
items.detail: Same mechanics plus LLP wind-down at Companies House

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll work through each route with worked examples, and the partnership agreement amendments you'll need before the transition.

scenes.heading: First-Year Filings: Compliance Calendar
scenes.subheading: Year one brings many registrations, deadlines and authorities, all overlapping
scenes.narration: Every new UK business faces a year-one filing avalanche, with several registrations, deadlines and authorities all overlapping. Miss any one of them and penalties trigger automatically.

scenes.heading: Sole trader: year one
scenes.narration: For a sole trader, register by the fifth of October, then file the first tax return about fifteen months later. The balancing payment and first payment on account fall on the same day, with the second in July.

items.label: Register with form CWF1
items.detail: Registration comes before any tax return

items.label: First SA100 and SA103
items.detail: Around 15 months later

items.label: Balance and first POA
items.detail: Paid the same day as the return

scenes.heading: Ltd company formed 1 Jan 2025
scenes.narration: Take a limited company incorporated on the first of January 2025. Its confirmation statement, first accounts and corporation tax deadlines all run on different clocks, alongside payroll and VAT duties.

items.label: First accounts
items.detail: 21 months from incorporation

items.label: CT600 and CT payment
items.detail: Filed 12 months, paid 9 months and a day after period end

items.label: Plus other duties
items.detail: Directors' SA100s, PAYE and RTI from month 1, VAT quarters

scenes.heading: Partnerships, LLPs and charities
scenes.narration: Partnerships and LLPs file a partnership return plus each member's own pages, and LLPs also file at Companies House. Charities report to the Charity Commission.

items.label: Partnership return
items.detail: Plus SA104 inside each member's SA100

items.label: LLP at Companies House
items.detail: LLP CS01 and LLP accounts

items.label: Charity Commission
items.detail: Annual return, accounts and trustees' report

scenes.heading: Critical year-one traps
scenes.narration: Watch out: registration deadlines arrive before tax-year deadlines, a company's long first accounts period splits into two periods for corporation tax, and directors' returns are separate from the company's.

items.label: Registrations come first
items.detail: CWF1 by 5 Oct, VAT within 30 days, PAYE before payday

items.label: Long first period
items.detail: Split into two accounting periods for CT

items.label: Separate returns, staff
items.detail: Director SA100 apart from CT600; auto-enrol from day 1

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module you'll build the compliance calendar for each entity type, set up a deadline tracker, and plan how to escalate issues during year one.

scenes.heading: Sole Trader Cessation
scenes.subheading: Simple mechanics, but rich in tax points for the final return
scenes.narration: Closing down a sole trader business is mechanically simple, but it is rich in tax points. Getting the final return right can make a real difference to your client.

scenes.heading: Why a Trade Ceases
scenes.narration: Traders stop for many reasons: retirement, ill-health, business failure, a sale to a third party, incorporation, or the death of the trader. Incorporation is covered separately in Module 55.

items.label: Retirement or ill-health
items.detail: The trader steps away from the business

items.label: Business failure
items.detail: The trade is no longer viable

items.label: Sale or incorporation
items.detail: Incorporation is covered in Module 55

items.label: Death of trader
items.detail: The trade ends on the trader's death

scenes.heading: Winding Down the Business
scenes.narration: Work through the business in order: dispose of or transfer stock, collect or write off debtors, settle creditors, then dispose of plant and machinery with balancing entries.

items.label: Stock
items.detail: Disposed of or transferred

items.label: Debtors
items.detail: Collected or written off

items.label: Creditors
items.detail: Settled in full

items.label: Plant and machinery
items.detail: Disposed of, with balancing entries

scenes.heading: Closing Formalities
scenes.narration: Next, deregister for VAT on form VAT7 within 30 days of ceasing, notify HMRC, file the final SA103 and SA100, close the business bank account, and keep records for at least 5 years.

items.label: VAT deregistration
items.detail: Form VAT7, within 30 days of ceasing

items.label: Notify HMRC
items.detail: Tell HMRC the trade has ceased

items.label: Final SA103 and SA100
items.detail: Tick ceased trading and give the date

items.label: Keep records
items.detail: After closing the business bank account

scenes.heading: Special Items in the Final Year
scenes.narration: The final return brings special items: a balancing charge or allowance on plant and machinery, terminal loss relief, post-cessation receipts taxed in the year received, plus National Insurance adjustments and any final PAYE.

items.label: Balancing charge
items.detail: Or allowance, on plant and machinery, CAA 2001

items.label: Terminal loss relief
items.detail: 3-year carry-back, ITA 2007

items.label: Post-cessation receipts
items.detail: Taxed in the year received, ITA 2007

items.label: NIC and final PAYE
items.detail: National Insurance adjustments; PAYE if any

scenes.heading: Terminal Loss: A Retiree
scenes.narration: The terminal loss covers the 12 months before cessation and can be set against the prior 3 years of taxable income. That is often valuable for retirees who had strong earlier years.

items.label: Strong earlier years
items.detail: A trader earned well in the years before retiring

items.label: Final 12 months
items.detail: A loss arises in the year before cessation

items.label: Carry back
items.detail: Offset against the prior 3 years' taxable income

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover each cessation step, the mechanics of the special items, and the year of cessation pro-forma.

scenes.heading: Partnership Cessation
scenes.subheading: Winding up the partnership and each partner's own cessation event
scenes.narration: Welcome to partnership cessation. It works in layers: the partnership winds up, and each partner has their own cessation event too, so getting both right matters.

scenes.heading: The layers of cessation
scenes.narration: The partnership files a final SA800 with the cessation flag and its tax reference is deregistered. Each partner files a final SA104 in their own return, and for LLPs there's a third layer at Companies House.

items.label: Partnership level
items.detail: Final SA800 with cessation flag; partnership UTR deregistered

items.label: Partner level
items.detail: Final SA104 in each partner's SA100; own terminal loss relief

items.label: LLP level
items.detail: LL DS01 strike-off or formal liquidation at Companies House

scenes.heading: Continuation vs cessation
scenes.narration: This test decides which path applies. If one partner retires but at least one partner carries on, it is not a cessation; if all partners leave and the business stops, it is a full dissolution.

items.label: Partial change
items.detail: One retires, others continue: not a cessation

items.label: Full dissolution
items.detail: All partners leave and the business stops

scenes.heading: Buyout to sole trader
scenes.narration: Here's a common scenario. When one partner buys out the others, the partnership ceases and a sole trader emerges; conversion to a limited company is covered separately in Module 56.

items.label: One partner buys out others
items.detail: The remaining owner takes over the business

items.label: Partnership ceases
items.detail: Partnership-level cessation steps apply

items.label: Sole trader emerges
items.detail: The business continues under one owner

scenes.heading: Settling capital accounts
scenes.narration: Each partner is paid their capital, reserves and share of goodwill, often in phases. Capital Gains Tax applies to that disposal, and Business Asset Disposal Relief may be available.

items.label: Pay out each partner
items.detail: Capital plus reserves plus share of goodwill, often phased

items.label: Consider CGT
items.detail: Disposal of capital interest is chargeable

items.label: Check BADR
items.detail: 2-year ownership and whole or most of business interest

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: We'll walk through partnership-level and per-partner mechanics, LLP wind-down, and the continuation test. Remember terminal loss relief under section 89 applies to each partner separately, and VAT, PAYE and register deregistrations are all required.

scenes.heading: Ltd Strike-Off: Voluntary Dissolution
scenes.subheading: Closing a solvent, simple Ltd company with form DS01
scenes.narration: Welcome to Module 60. Voluntary strike-off using form DS01, under section 1003 of the Companies Act 2006, is the cheapest and simplest way to close a limited company.

scenes.heading: Strike-Off at a Glance
scenes.narration: It costs just £33 to file with Companies House, followed by a public notice period of two to three months. Keep the £25k reserves limit in mind, as it decides whether this route suits your client.

items.label: Companies House fee
items.detail: Filing form DS01

items.label: Public notice period
items.detail: Before dissolution

items.label: Distributable reserves cap
items.detail: Over this, an MVL is needed instead

scenes.heading: Who Can Use DS01?
scenes.narration: Strike-off is strictly for solvent companies with simple affairs. The company must not have traded or changed its name in the last three months, and must have no pending insolvency, company voluntary arrangement or creditor agreements.

items.label: No recent trading
items.detail: Nor a name change in that period

items.label: No insolvency pending
items.detail: Company must be solvent

items.label: No CVA
items.detail: No company voluntary arrangement

items.label: No creditor agreements
items.detail: Affairs must be simple

scenes.heading: The Five-Step Process
scenes.narration: First clear creditors and tax, then distribute reserves, file DS01 and copy it to interested parties, wait out the objection window, and receive confirmation. Directors' duties continue throughout.

items.label: Clear liabilities
items.detail: Pay creditors and tax liabilities

items.label: Distribute reserves
items.detail: Pay out remaining reserves to shareholders

items.label: File DS01
items.detail: Copy to creditors, staff, shareholders, pension trustees

items.label: Objection window
items.detail: Wait for any objections

items.label: Strike-off confirmed
items.detail: Company is dissolved

scenes.heading: Watch the Limits
scenes.narration: Reserves over £25k mean a members' voluntary liquidation is needed instead. And the targeted anti-avoidance rule catches phoenix arrangements, where shareholders restart the same trade within two years.

items.label: Reserves over the cap
items.detail: Use an MVL, covered in Module 61

items.label: Phoenix arrangements
items.detail: Restarting the same trade triggers anti-avoidance

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: We'll work through eligibility, the £25k cap, Business Asset Disposal Relief, anti-phoenix rules, what happens to missed assets after dissolution, and how to choose between strike-off and liquidation.

scenes.heading: Members' Voluntary Liquidation
scenes.subheading: The tax-efficient exit for solvent companies with reserves above £25k
scenes.narration: A Members' Voluntary Liquidation is the tax-efficient way to close a solvent company with reserves above the twenty-five thousand pound strike-off cap. It can save shareholders a lot of tax.

scenes.heading: Capital, not income
scenes.narration: In a liquidation, all distributions to shareholders are treated as capital, not income. That means Business Asset Disposal Relief rates apply instead of dividend tax rates of 33.75 to 39.35 percent.

items.label: Business Asset Disposal
items.detail: Rising to 14% April 2025, 18% April 2026

items.label: Dividend tax
items.detail: What reserves would face if paid as income

scenes.heading: What it can be worth
scenes.narration: On five hundred thousand pounds of reserves, that's roughly one hundred thousand pounds saved. Insolvency practitioner fees are typically three to seven thousand, so it's worth it when the savings exceed the fees.

items.label: Reserves
items.detail: Example level of company reserves

items.label: Approximate saving
items.detail: Relief rates versus dividend tax

items.label: Typical IP fees
items.detail: Worth it if savings exceed the fees

scenes.heading: The MVL process
scenes.narration: Directors sign a Declaration of Solvency, shareholders pass the resolution, and an insolvency practitioner is appointed as liquidator. It typically takes two to six months, longer if HMRC clearance is needed.

items.label: Declaration of Solvency
items.detail: Directors confirm debts paid within 12 months

items.label: Wind-up resolution
items.detail: Passed by 75% of shareholders

items.label: Appoint liquidator
items.detail: An Insolvency Practitioner takes control

items.label: Settle and distribute
items.detail: Creditors paid, net assets go to shareholders

scenes.heading: Risks to watch
scenes.narration: Watch the anti-avoidance rule in section 396B: carrying on the same trade within two years turns the distribution into a dividend and kills the relief. And a false Declaration of Solvency is a criminal offence.

items.label: TAAR, ITTOIA s.396B
items.detail: Same trade recharacterises distribution as dividend

items.label: False declaration
items.detail: Debts must be payable within 12 months

scenes.heading: Pre-MVL planning
scenes.narration: Good preparation matters. Before the liquidation, clear directors' loan accounts, recover any research and development refunds, and manage the employment status of director-shareholders.

items.label: Clear director loans
items.detail: Settle directors' loan accounts first

items.label: Recover R&D refunds
items.detail: Collect research and development refunds

items.label: Employment status
items.detail: Manage status of director-shareholders

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover eligibility, appointing the insolvency practitioner, the twenty-five thousand pound decision versus strike-off, avoiding the anti-avoidance rule, relief mechanics, and post-liquidation compliance.

scenes.heading: Creditors' Voluntary Liquidation
scenes.subheading: The insolvent company exit, chosen by directors before creditors force it
scenes.narration: A creditors' voluntary liquidation is how directors choose to close an insolvent company, rather than waiting for a creditor to petition for compulsory liquidation under section 124 of the Insolvency Act 1986.

scenes.heading: Two Insolvency Tests
scenes.narration: A company is insolvent on either test: the cash-flow test, where it can't pay debts as they fall due, or the balance-sheet test, where liabilities exceed assets.

items.label: Cash-flow test
items.detail: Can't pay debts as they fall due

items.label: Balance-sheet test
items.detail: Liabilities exceed assets

scenes.heading: Timing Is Critical
scenes.narration: From the moment of insolvency, wrongful trading liability under section 214 begins. Directors who keep trading with no reasonable prospect of avoiding liquidation can be personally liable for the extra losses.

items.label: Wrongful trading
items.detail: Personal liability for additional losses

scenes.heading: The CVL Process
scenes.narration: Directors hold a board meeting and appoint an insolvency practitioner. Shareholders need 75 percent to wind up, then creditors meet within 14 days and their nominated practitioner becomes liquidator.

items.label: Board meeting
items.detail: Directors decide to act

items.label: Appoint IP
items.detail: Insolvency practitioner engaged

items.label: Shareholders' meeting
items.detail: Majority needed to wind up

items.label: Creditors' meeting
items.detail: Held within 14 days under s.100

items.label: Liquidator appointed
items.detail: IP nominated by creditors

scenes.heading: Director Conduct Review
scenes.narration: After the liquidation, directors' conduct is reviewed. Breaches like these can lead to personal liability and disqualification for up to 15 years under the Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986.

items.label: Wrongful trading
items.detail: Trading on with no reasonable prospect

items.label: Fraudulent trading
items.detail: Breach of duty reviewed

items.label: Preference payments
items.detail: Breach of duty reviewed

items.label: Transactions at undervalue
items.detail: Breach of duty reviewed

scenes.heading: Key Figures and HMRC Priority
scenes.narration: Disqualification can last up to 15 years. And since 1 December 2020, His Majesty's Revenue and Customs is a preferential creditor for VAT, PAYE, national insurance and CIS, ranking ahead of floating-charge holders.

items.label: Maximum disqualification
items.detail: Under CDDA 1986

items.label: HMRC preferential status
items.detail: VAT, PAYE/NIC, CIS ahead of floating charges

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll walk through the insolvency tests, the timing-critical director duties, the CVL process, and the disqualification risks after a CVL.

scenes.heading: Compulsory Liquidation
scenes.subheading: Court-ordered winding up, triggered by a winding-up petition
scenes.narration: Compulsory liquidation is a court-ordered winding up, the involuntary version of a creditors' voluntary liquidation. It starts with a winding-up petition under section 122 of the Insolvency Act 1986.

scenes.heading: Grounds for a Creditor Petition
scenes.narration: The most common petitioner is a creditor. Any debt over seven hundred and fifty pounds, plus a statutory demand left unpaid for twenty-one days, gives grounds for a petition.

items.label: Minimum debt
items.detail: Any debt above this amount

items.label: Statutory demand unpaid
items.detail: Then the creditor can petition

scenes.heading: Who Else Can Petition?
scenes.narration: Others can petition too: the company itself, though that's rare as a voluntary liquidation is faster, directors jointly, shareholders on the just-and-equitable ground, HMRC, and the Secretary of State.

items.label: Company or directors
items.detail: Company rarely; directors jointly

items.label: Shareholders
items.detail: Under the just-and-equitable ground

items.label: HMRC
items.detail: For significant tax debt

items.label: Secretary of State
items.detail: Public interest under CDDA 1986

scenes.heading: From Petition to Liquidator
scenes.narration: The petition is filed at the High Court, or county court for smaller companies, advertised in The Gazette, and heard within about eight weeks. The court appoints the Official Receiver, who may then appoint a private insolvency practitioner.

items.label: Petition filed
items.detail: High Court, or county court for smaller firms

items.label: Advertised
items.detail: Published in The Gazette

items.label: Hearing
items.detail: Court makes the liquidation order

items.label: Official Receiver appointed
items.detail: May then appoint a private IP

scenes.heading: The Freeze After a Petition
scenes.narration: Between petition and order, assets are effectively frozen and transactions can be voided under section 127. Directors have a twenty-one day window to convert to a voluntary liquidation or otherwise dispose.

items.label: Window to act
items.detail: Directors can convert to CVL or otherwise dispose

items.label: Transactions voidable
items.detail: Assets effectively frozen; banks often freeze accounts

items.label: Tougher conduct review
items.detail: Typically more aggressive than in a CVL

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: Afterwards the same regime as a voluntary liquidation applies. In this module we'll cover petition mechanics, the section 127 freeze, conversion options, the Official Receiver's role, and what to do when a petition arrives.

scenes.heading: Administration & CVA
scenes.subheading: Rescue tools: alternatives to liquidation when a business has rescuable value
scenes.narration: Administration and Company Voluntary Arrangements are the rescue tools. They are alternatives to liquidation when a business still has value worth saving.

scenes.heading: Administration: the moratorium
scenes.narration: Under Schedule B1 of the Insolvency Act 1986, a licensed insolvency practitioner takes control under court protection. The big benefit is the moratorium, which halts creditor action.

items.label: Creditor action halted
items.detail: Court protection while the administrator acts

items.label: No winding-up petition
items.detail: A petition cannot be presented

items.label: Security not enforced
items.detail: Not without consent

scenes.heading: Three ranked statutory purposes
scenes.narration: The administrator must aim for these purposes in order. Rescue as a going concern comes first, then a better result than liquidation, then realising property for secured or preferential creditors.

items.label: Rescue going concern
items.detail: Save the company itself

items.label: Beat liquidation
items.detail: Better result for creditors as a whole

items.label: Realise property
items.detail: Distribute to secured or preferential creditors

scenes.heading: CVA: a deal with creditors
scenes.narration: A Company Voluntary Arrangement, under Part 1 of the Act, typically pays a reduced amount over three to five years. It needs 75 percent by value of creditors, and trading continues throughout.

items.label: Typical repayment term
items.detail: Reduced amount instead of the full debt

items.label: Approval threshold
items.detail: By value of creditors

items.label: Part A1 moratorium
items.detail: Introduced by CIGA 2020; otherwise no moratorium

scenes.heading: CIGA 2020 tools and pre-packs
scenes.narration: The Corporate Insolvency and Governance Act 2020 added the Restructuring Plan for larger cases. Pre-pack sales, often to connected parties, need a SIP 16 statement and a viability statement.

items.label: Restructuring Plan
items.detail: Companies Act 2006; cross-class cramdown

items.label: Pre-pack administration
items.detail: Plus viability statement under SoCV regulations 2021

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we cover how administration works, how a CVA is structured, the CIGA 2020 changes, and when each rescue tool applies.

scenes.heading: Final Accounts on Cessation
scenes.subheading: Why the break-up basis replaces going concern when a business stops
scenes.narration: When a business ceases, its final accounts differ from ordinary year-end accounts in critical ways. The going-concern basis no longer applies, so everything is measured differently.

scenes.heading: Going Concern vs Break-Up Basis
scenes.narration: Under FRS 102 section 3.9, the break-up basis is required. Assets go in at net realisable value, and liabilities at the amount needed to settle them.

items.label: Assets
items.detail: Measured at net realisable value

items.label: Liabilities
items.detail: Measured at settlement amount

scenes.heading: Sole Traders and Partnerships
scenes.narration: For unincorporated businesses, closing stock goes in at market value, and disposed plant and machinery needs balancing capital allowance entries. Debtors are shown at recoverable value, and partnership capital accounts are settled.

items.label: Closing stock
items.detail: Valued at market value

items.label: Plant and machinery
items.detail: Balancing capital allowance entries

items.label: Debtors
items.detail: Recoverable value; write off uncollectible

items.label: Partner capital
items.detail: Capital accounts settled

scenes.heading: Limited Company Final Accounts
scenes.narration: For limited companies, prepare accounts to the cessation date, often mid-year, and include the final accounting period for the CT600. Reverse deferred tax, since there are no future profits, and explain the basis in a going-concern note.

items.label: Prepare to cessation date
items.detail: Often mid-year; final period for CT600

items.label: Label the balance sheet
items.detail: Prepared on a break-up basis, if appropriate

items.label: Reverse deferred tax
items.detail: No future profits to use it against

items.label: Add going-concern note
items.detail: Explains the cessation basis

scenes.heading: Provisions and Write-Downs
scenes.narration: Recognise cessation-cost provisions, such as redundancy once a constructive obligation arises, lease exit, dilapidations, warranties and contract termination. Impair goodwill, intangibles and property, plant and equipment to recoverable amount.

items.label: Redundancy
items.detail: When constructive obligation arises, FRS 102 s.21

items.label: Lease exit and warranties
items.detail: Dilapidations, warranty and contract termination

items.label: Asset impairment
items.detail: Goodwill, intangibles, PP&E to recoverable amount

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll walk through the break-up basis, the required disclosures, what it means for the auditor, usually an emphasis of matter paragraph, and the bridge to closing the tax returns.

scenes.heading: Capital Distributions & BADR
scenes.subheading: How closing a company is taxed can change the owner's bill dramatically
scenes.narration: When a company closes, whether distributions are taxed as capital or income decides the tax bill, potentially saving owners 40% of every pound distributed.

scenes.heading: Capital vs Income Treatment
scenes.narration: Capital treatment, at 10% with Business Asset Disposal Relief up to £1m or 18% without it, beats dividend tax of 33.75 to 39.35% at all but the lowest income bands.

items.label: Capital treatment
items.detail: 10% with BADR up to £1m, 18% without

items.label: Dividend treatment
items.detail: Income tax on distributions as dividends

scenes.heading: Choosing the Closure Route
scenes.narration: Each route treats distributions differently. Strike-off is capital only up to £25k, while a members' voluntary liquidation gives full capital treatment with relief, subject to the anti-avoidance rule.

items.label: Strike-off DS01
items.detail: Capital up to £25k, income above (s.1030A)

items.label: MVL
items.detail: Full capital with BADR, subject to s.396B TAAR

items.label: Share buy-back
items.detail: Capital if CTA 2010 s.1033-1043 conditions met

items.label: Liquidation in a sale
items.detail: Capital treatment

scenes.heading: BADR Rates Are Rising
scenes.narration: The relief's rate is 10% now, rising to 14% from 6 April 2025 and 18% from 6 April 2026, with a £1m lifetime limit, so timing really matters.

items.label: Current rate
items.detail: 10%, lifetime limit £1m

items.label: First rise
items.detail: Rate rises to 14%

items.label: Second rise
items.detail: Rate rises to 18%

scenes.heading: The TAAR Trap
scenes.narration: Under the targeted anti-avoidance rule in section 396B, carrying on the same trade within 2 years turns the distribution into a dividend, killing the relief.

items.label: Same trade within 2 years
items.detail: Capital becomes dividend; BADR lost

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: We'll cover each route, how the relief works including the 2-year, 5% and officer conditions, avoiding the anti-avoidance rule with a clean break, timing before the rate rises, and a practical decision framework.

scenes.heading: Disincorporation: Ltd to Sole Trader
scenes.subheading: A rare but tax-expensive transition that often catches advisors out
scenes.narration: Disincorporation means reversing a limited company back to a sole trader. It's rare, but it can be very tax-expensive, which is exactly why it catches advisors out.

scenes.heading: Why clients disincorporate
scenes.narration: Clients usually want out because they're tired of the admin, profits have dropped below break-even, incorporation simply didn't suit them, or regulations have changed.

items.label: Simplification
items.detail: Tired of corporation tax, accounts and filings

items.label: Profits fell
items.detail: Dropped below break-even, covered in Module 49

items.label: Didn't suit them
items.detail: Client decided incorporation wasn't right

items.label: Regulatory change
items.detail: New rules change the picture

scenes.heading: No reverse incorporation relief
scenes.narration: The big problem is that there's no reverse version of section 162 incorporation relief. The 2013 Disincorporation Relief only ran from 2013 to 2018, was never extended, and isn't available now.

items.label: No s.162 in reverse
items.detail: Nothing defers gains on the way out

items.label: FA 2013 relief expired
items.detail: Never extended, not available now

scenes.heading: What disincorporation triggers
scenes.narration: Expect capital gains tax on assets passed out at market value, a balancing charge on plant and machinery, and income tax on reserves as dividends. VAT transfer of a going concern and Business Asset Disposal Relief apply only if conditions are met.

items.label: CGT at market value
items.detail: On company assets transferred to the shareholder

items.label: Balancing charge
items.detail: On plant and machinery, CAA 2001 s.55

items.label: Income tax
items.detail: Undistributed reserves taxed as dividends

items.label: TOGC and BADR
items.detail: Only available if conditions are met

scenes.heading: Order of operations
scenes.narration: Order matters: clear director's loan accounts, distribute reserves, transfer assets at market value, cease the company's trade, close it by strike-off or members' voluntary liquidation, then register as a sole trader.

items.label: Clear DLAs
items.detail: Settle director's loan accounts

items.label: Distribute reserves
items.detail: Pay out distributable reserves

items.label: Transfer assets at MV
items.detail: Move assets to the shareholder at market value

items.label: Cease trade and close
items.detail: Stop Ltd trade, then strike-off or MVL

items.label: Register sole trader
items.detail: Using form CWF1

scenes.heading: Is it worth it?
scenes.narration: Often the tax cost of disincorporating outweighs the long-term compliance saving, so many clients keep a dormant company or switch it to non-trading instead.

items.label: Disincorporate
items.detail: Tax cost often exceeds compliance savings

items.label: Keep the Ltd
items.detail: Make it dormant or non-trading instead

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover the mechanics, the missing reverse relief, a practical decision tree, and alternatives like dormancy.

scenes.heading: Sole Trader to Partnership
scenes.subheading: The tax-light transition: both regimes are tax-transparent and both file SA
scenes.narration: Moving from sole trader to partnership is the tax-light transition. Both are tax-transparent and both file Self Assessment, but there are still key tax points to get right.

scenes.heading: Cessation Meets Commencement
scenes.narration: For tax, the sole trade ceases and a partnership trade begins. But basis-period continuation generally applies, so no balancing charges arise if assets pass at carrying value.

items.label: Treated as
items.detail: Cessation of sole trade plus start of partnership trade

items.label: In practice
items.detail: Basis continuation; no balancing charges at carrying value

scenes.heading: Watch the Goodwill
scenes.narration: The incoming partner acquires a share of goodwill at market value. If the original sole trader receives market-value consideration, there may be Capital Gains Tax to pay.

items.label: Potential CGT
items.detail: If sole trader receives market-value consideration

scenes.heading: The 5 Setup Steps
scenes.narration: Draft the Partnership Agreement, register the partnership on form SA400, register each new partner on SA401, nominate a partner to file the SA800, then update the VAT registration.

items.label: Partnership Agreement
items.detail: Profit sharing, salaries, drawings, disputes

items.label: Register via SA400
items.detail: Partnership gets its own UTR

items.label: Partners file SA401
items.detail: Each new partner registers for individual SA

items.label: Nominate SA800 filer
items.detail: One partner files the partnership return

items.label: Update VAT
items.detail: VAT68 transfer or a new registration

scenes.heading: Returns Across the Changeover
scenes.narration: A final SA103 closes the sole trade, then the first SA800 is filed with SA104s for every partner. Basis-period reform from Module 42 means the tax-year basis applies from 2024 to 25.

items.label: Final SA103
items.detail: Closes the unincorporated sole trade

items.label: First SA800 and SA104s
items.detail: Partnership return plus one SA104 per partner

items.label: Tax-year basis
items.detail: Basis-period reform, see Module 42

scenes.heading: Common Scenarios
scenes.narration: You'll often see a spouse or child brought in for income-splitting, a partner joining to inject capital, or a professional firm formalising an existing arrangement.

items.label: Spouse or child
items.detail: Income-splitting

items.label: Capital partner
items.detail: New partner brings a capital injection

items.label: Professional firm
items.detail: Formalising an existing arrangement

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover the transition mechanics, how goodwill works, basis continuation, and the Partnership Agreement essentials.

scenes.heading: Partnership to Ltd: Quick Recap
scenes.subheading: Partner-specific mechanics of incorporating a partnership, cross-ref Module 56
scenes.narration: This module is a quick-reference recap of moving a partnership into a limited company. Module 56 covers the route in depth; here we focus on what each partner needs to know.

scenes.heading: Capital Gains Tax Reliefs
scenes.narration: Each partner makes a capital gains tax disposal of their partnership interest, with goodwill, premises and intangibles moving to the company at market value. These reliefs can soften the impact.

items.label: Section 162
items.detail: Incorporation relief defers CGT if paid wholly in shares

items.label: Section 165
items.detail: Gift relief available where shares are gifted

items.label: BADR
items.detail: May cover any taxable element; rising to 14% then 18%

scenes.heading: The Incorporation Process
scenes.narration: File the final partnership return, set up the company with shares matching each partner's old share, then transfer the assets and goodwill under a sale agreement, with TUPE for staff and a VAT transfer of a going concern.

items.label: Final SA800
items.detail: Cessation return with all partners' allocations

items.label: Incorporate Ltd
items.detail: Shares per each partner's pre-incorporation share

items.label: Sale agreement
items.detail: Transfers assets and goodwill; TUPE for employees

items.label: VAT TOGC
items.detail: Transfer of a going concern for VAT

items.label: Close down
items.detail: Deregister partnership UTR; each partner files SA104

scenes.heading: Critical Timing Points
scenes.narration: Timing matters. Aligning the partnership year-end with the incorporation date simplifies the final allocation, and you should consider the basis-period reform position and, for an LLP, strike-off.

items.label: Align year-end
items.detail: Match partnership year-end to incorporation date

items.label: Basis-period reform
items.detail: Consider each partner's position

items.label: LLP wind-down
items.detail: Strike-off at Companies House if an LLP

scenes.heading: Settling Capital Accounts
scenes.narration: Losses can carry forward into the company under section 86 of the Corporation Tax Act 2010 if the same trade continues. Capital accounts can be settled before or after incorporation, each with its own advantage.

items.label: Before incorporation
items.detail: Better for a clean ledger

items.label: After incorporation
items.detail: Can work as a director's loan account credit

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: So, here's the structure we'll sketch. For the deeper mechanics, head back to Module 56.

scenes.heading: Group Restructuring
scenes.subheading: Holding companies, subsidiaries and the tax reliefs that make groups work
scenes.narration: Welcome to Module 70 on group restructuring. A holding company with several subsidiaries can separate risk, keep sale options open, support tax planning and split up operations.

scenes.heading: Typical group patterns
scenes.narration: You'll see a few common shapes in practice: a holding company over trading, intellectual property and property subsidiaries, a trading group with separate brand entities, or a family investment company over a trading subsidiary.

items.label: HoldCo + specialist subs
items.detail: Trading, intellectual property and property subsidiaries

items.label: Brand entities
items.detail: Trading group with separate brand companies

items.label: Family investment co
items.detail: Family investment company plus trading subsidiary

scenes.heading: Substantial Shareholding Exemption
scenes.narration: The Substantial Shareholding Exemption is effectively the capital gains exemption for groups on disposals of trading company shares. It needs a holding of at least 10 percent, held for at least 12 months.

items.label: Minimum shareholding
items.detail: Shares in a trading company

items.label: Minimum holding period
items.detail: Under TCGA Schedule 7AC

scenes.heading: Other key group reliefs
scenes.narration: Group relief lets trading losses be shared, assets can move within the group at no gain and no loss, group transfers can get Stamp Duty Land Tax relief, and a VAT group simplifies supplies between members.

items.label: Group relief
items.detail: Trading losses, CTA 2010 Part 5

items.label: No gain/no loss transfers
items.detail: Move assets without CGT, TCGA s.171

items.label: SDLT group relief
items.detail: Finance Act 2003 Schedule 7

items.label: VAT group registration
items.detail: Simplifies intra-group supplies

scenes.heading: Anti-avoidance traps
scenes.narration: Watch for the traps. The exemption's trading test fails if non-trading activities exceed 20 percent, and depreciatory transaction and transfer pricing rules also apply to connected companies.

items.label: SSE trading test
items.detail: Non-trading activities must not exceed 20%

items.label: Depreciatory transactions
items.detail: Rules targeting value-shifting within groups

items.label: Transfer pricing
items.detail: Applies to connected company transactions

scenes.heading: Setting up a holding company
scenes.narration: You can insert a holding company by a share-for-share exchange, or by direct subscription. Be careful with subscription, as paying for shares in cash can raise a Stamp Duty Land Tax issue.

items.label: Share-for-share exchange
items.detail: TCGA s.135 and s.136, plus CTA s.110

items.label: Direct subscription
items.detail: SDLT issue if shares are paid in cash

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover group structures, the major reliefs, the exemption conditions, intra-group transfers, VAT grouping and demerger options, which are explored further in Module 73.

scenes.heading: Ltd to Charity or CIO Conversion
scenes.subheading: How a trading Ltd becomes a registered charity, and what changes
scenes.narration: This is the mission-shift transition, where a trading limited company becomes a registered charity. Owners do it to access tax exemption, Gift Aid, grant funding eligibility and legacies.

scenes.heading: Two Routes to Charity Status
scenes.narration: You can convert the existing company into a company limited by guarantee, or incorporate a new charitable incorporated organisation and transfer the trade. The second is simpler and commonly preferred since 2013.

items.label: Convert Ltd to CLG
items.detail: Charitable articles, register with CC and HMRC; court order?

items.label: New CIO plus trade transfer
items.detail: Simpler; common preferred route post-2013

scenes.heading: The Critical Issue: No Private Benefit
scenes.narration: Here is the big one. Once converted, existing shareholders cannot benefit, because a charitable purpose means no private benefit at all.

items.label: Shareholders cannot benefit
items.detail: Charitable purpose means no private benefit

scenes.heading: Tax Reliefs on Transfer
scenes.narration: Founders giving shares to the charity get gift-to-charity relief, so no Capital Gains Tax, plus income tax relief. Property transferred for charitable purposes can get Stamp Duty Land Tax relief.

items.label: No CGT on share gift
items.detail: Gift-to-charity relief for founders

items.label: Income tax relief
items.detail: Relief for the donor on shares given

items.label: SDLT relief
items.detail: Property transferred for charitable purposes

scenes.heading: Assets, Trustees and Compliance
scenes.narration: Structure the asset transfer carefully to protect charity tax status, often keeping a trading subsidiary. Then appoint fit-and-proper trustees and switch to Charity Commission returns and SORP accounts.

items.label: Transfer assets to CIO
items.detail: Structured to keep HMRC charity tax status

items.label: Keep trading subsidiary
items.detail: Often retained for revenue-generating work

items.label: Appoint trustees
items.detail: Must pass the fit-and-proper test

items.label: Switch compliance
items.detail: From CT600 and CH accounts to CC return and SORP

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: We will cover both routes, the share-disposal mechanics, the asset transfer, VAT points like partial exemption and reduced rates, and the year-one compliance calendar.

scenes.heading: Sale of a Business: Assets or Shares?
scenes.subheading: The most consequential structuring choice for both buyer and seller
scenes.narration: Welcome to Module 72. Whether a business is sold as an asset sale or a share sale shapes the tax cost, the deal complexity, who takes on the liabilities, and how the price is paid.

scenes.heading: Two Ways to Sell
scenes.narration: In an asset sale, the buyer picks specific assets and liabilities, and the seller's company keeps everything else. In a share sale, the buyer takes the whole company, including all its liabilities.

items.label: Asset sale
items.detail: Buyer cherry-picks assets and assumes chosen liabilities

items.label: Share sale
items.detail: Buyer acquires the company with all assets and liabilities

scenes.heading: Tax on an Asset Sale
scenes.narration: The seller faces double tax: corporation tax on gains inside the company, then tax again when extracting the cash. The buyer, though, gets a step-up in base costs and valuable deductions.

items.label: Seller: double tax
items.detail: Corporation tax in the company, then tax on extraction

items.label: Buyer: step-up
items.detail: Higher base costs on the assets acquired

items.label: Buyer: new allowance pools
items.detail: Fresh capital allowance pools on plant

items.label: Buyer: goodwill relief
items.detail: Amortisation deduction for post-1 April 2002 goodwill

scenes.heading: Tax on a Share Sale
scenes.narration: The seller pays capital gains tax once, and Business Asset Disposal Relief may apply. The buyer inherits historic base costs with no step-up, but avoids double tax. A corporate seller may use the Substantial Shareholding Exemption from Module 70.

items.label: Seller
items.detail: Single tax: CGT on shares, BADR available

items.label: Buyer
items.detail: Historic base costs, no step-up, no double tax

scenes.heading: Who Prefers What, and Deal Tools
scenes.narration: Buyers usually prefer an asset sale for control and no historic liabilities, while sellers prefer a share sale for a cleaner exit. Warranties, indemnities, escrow and earn-outs help bridge the gap.

items.label: Buyer prefers assets
items.detail: Control, step-up, no historic liabilities

items.label: Seller prefers shares
items.detail: Cleaner exit, single tax, BADR

items.label: Protection
items.detail: Warranties, indemnities, escrow

items.label: Pricing mechanics
items.detail: Completion accounts, locked-box, deferred, earn-outs

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: We'll compare the two routes, work through the tax and deal mechanics, including stamp duty land tax and VAT transfer of a going concern, and explore the negotiation tension between buyer and seller.

scenes.heading: Demergers
scenes.subheading: Splitting one corporate group into two or more independently owned entities
scenes.narration: A demerger splits a single corporate group into two or more independently owned entities. Getting the structure right matters, because the tax treatment depends on careful planning.

scenes.heading: Why groups demerge
scenes.narration: Groups usually demerge to separate trading and investment activities, prepare one business for sale, resolve shareholder disputes, or unlock substantial shareholding exemption eligibility.

items.label: Trading and investment
items.detail: Separate the two activities

items.label: Prepare for sale
items.detail: Ready one business for sale

items.label: Shareholder disputes
items.detail: Let parties go separate ways

items.label: Unlock SSE
items.detail: Substantial shareholding exemption eligibility

scenes.heading: Three statutory routes
scenes.narration: There are three statutory routes: a distribution in specie, a court-confirmed capital reduction, or a liquidation where assets pass to new holding companies under section 110 of the Insolvency Act 1986.

items.label: Distribution in specie
items.detail: CTA 2010 s.1075-1086: HoldCo gives sub shares to holders

items.label: Capital reduction
items.detail: CA 2006 s.641-653: court-confirmed demerger reserve

items.label: Liquidation demerger
items.detail: TCGA s.137: assets to new HoldCos via s.110 IA 1986

scenes.heading: Tax mechanics
scenes.narration: A distribution in specie is generally tax neutral if the conditions are met. Shareholders are treated as swapping their original shares for new ones, with the cost split between them, and HMRC clearance is mandatory.

items.label: Tax neutral
items.detail: If TCGA s.139 conditions are met

items.label: Cost basis split
items.detail: Deemed disposal and acquisition of shares

items.label: HMRC clearance
items.detail: Mandatory, via SP3/16 advance assurance

scenes.heading: Stamp taxes
scenes.narration: Stamp duty is usually relieved through reconstruction relief. Stamp duty land tax is relieved for group transfers if the companies are within a seventy-five percent group at the relevant times.

items.label: Stamp duty relief
items.detail: Reconstruction relief usually applies

items.label: SDLT group relief
items.detail: Group needed at the relevant times

scenes.heading: Anti-avoidance rules
scenes.narration: Watch the anti-avoidance rules. The transactions in securities rules and the targeted anti-avoidance rule can both catch a demerger that isn't properly structured.

items.label: Transactions in Securities
items.detail: Can counter tax advantages from share deals

items.label: TAAR
items.detail: Targeted anti-avoidance rule

scenes.heading: In this module
scenes.narration: In this module we'll sketch each route, the tax mechanics, clearance requirements and the typical demerger timeline, using common scenarios like family disputes and pre-sale splits.

scenes.heading: Reconstructions
scenes.subheading: Moving a trade and assets between companies without losing tax continuity
scenes.narration: A reconstruction moves a trade and its assets from one company to another, while the recipient carries on the same trade and the shareholders stay substantially identical. Done properly, tax continuity is kept.

scenes.heading: The reliefs that make it work
scenes.narration: Several reliefs work together. Corporation tax rules let the recipient inherit trading losses and capital allowances pools, and there is reconstruction relief for stamp duty, stamp duty land tax and capital gains tax.

items.label: Corporation tax continuity
items.detail: s.939 and s.940A-947: losses, allowances pools and more

items.label: Stamp duty
items.detail: Reconstruction relief on the share-for-share exchange

items.label: Stamp duty land tax
items.detail: Schedule 7 relief on property transfers

items.label: Capital gains tax
items.detail: Business reconstructions where shares are issued

scenes.heading: Conditions to qualify
scenes.narration: To qualify, the shareholders must be the same, the same trade must continue, the consideration must be substantially in shares, and there must be a commercial reason. Getting HMRC clearance under SP3/16 is advisable.

items.label: Same shareholders
items.detail: Ownership stays substantially identical

items.label: Same trade continues
items.detail: The recipient carries on the same trade

items.label: Paid in shares
items.detail: Consideration substantially in shares

items.label: Commercial reason
items.detail: A genuine business purpose

items.label: Seek HMRC clearance
items.detail: Clearance is advisable

scenes.heading: A typical hive-down before sale
scenes.narration: A common use is a hive-down: the trade moves into a new subsidiary before a sale. Groups also use reconstructions to move trades internally, reorganise before listing, or separate trade from non-trading assets.

items.label: Company wants to sell trade
items.detail: It plans a sale of one business line

items.label: Hive-down to new subsidiary
items.detail: Trade and assets move into a new sub

items.label: Tax position carried over
items.detail: Losses and allowances pools can follow the trade

items.label: New subsidiary is sold
items.detail: The buyer acquires the trade in a clean company

scenes.heading: Reconstruction or demerger?
scenes.narration: Don't confuse the two. In a reconstruction the trade moves but ownership doesn't change, so you keep a single-entity outcome, whereas a demerger creates separate ownerships.

items.label: Reconstruction
items.detail: Trade moves, ownership stays the same

items.label: Demerger
items.detail: Creates separate ownerships

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll work through the relief framework, the qualifying conditions, common scenarios, and finish with a hive-down and sale case study.

scenes.heading: IR35 and Off-Payroll Working
scenes.subheading: Stopping employee tax avoidance through Personal Service Companies
scenes.narration: IR35 is the UK's anti-avoidance regime. If a role would be employment without the Personal Service Company in the middle, full PAYE and National Insurance apply to the deemed employment income.

scenes.heading: How the Rules Developed
scenes.narration: IR35 began in the Finance Act 2000. The off-payroll rules then moved the status assessment and tax deduction onto the end client, first in the public sector, then for medium and large private businesses.

items.label: IR35 introduced
items.detail: Chapter 8 ITEPA 2003

items.label: Public sector shift
items.detail: End client assesses status and deducts tax

items.label: Private sector shift
items.detail: Medium and large private sector clients

scenes.heading: Who Decides Status?
scenes.narration: Size matters here. Small companies, measured under the Companies Act 2006, still use Chapter 8, so the Personal Service Company decides its own status. Otherwise the client decides under Chapter 10.

items.label: Small client
items.detail: PSC determines its own status

items.label: Medium or large client
items.detail: End client assesses and deducts tax

scenes.heading: The Employment Status Tests
scenes.narration: The status tests come from Ready Mixed Concrete in 1968. Look at mutuality of obligation, personal service and substitution, control, and other factors. HMRC's CEST tool gives a determination, sometimes binding.

items.label: Mutuality of obligation
items.detail: Duty to offer and accept work

items.label: Personal service
items.detail: Can a substitute be sent?

items.label: Control
items.detail: Who directs how the work is done

items.label: Other factors
items.detail: Financial risk, equipment, integration

scenes.heading: The Status Determination Statement
scenes.narration: The client must issue a Status Determination Statement to the Personal Service Company and the fee-payer, often the agency. It must arrive before the first payment and be reissued whenever things change.

items.label: Client decides status
items.detail: Assessment made by the end client

items.label: Issue the SDS
items.detail: To the PSC and the fee-payer

items.label: Before first payment
items.detail: Must be in place before paying

items.label: Reissue on change
items.detail: Update when the engagement changes

scenes.heading: Getting It Wrong
scenes.narration: Getting status wrong is costly. Deemed payments are triggered, PAYE and National Insurance become due, and interest plus penalties apply on any underpayment. Since 2021 many PSCs have closed and umbrella companies have grown.

items.label: Deemed payments
items.detail: Triggered on the engagement

items.label: PAYE and NIC due
items.detail: Full employee taxes on deemed income

items.label: Interest and penalties
items.detail: Charged on any underpayment

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover the legal framework, the status tests, how the statement works, the limits of CEST, and how the contractor market has shifted since 2021.

scenes.heading: Inheritance Tax
scenes.subheading: The UK charge on death estates and lifetime gifts within 7 years
scenes.narration: Inheritance Tax, or IHT, is the UK's charge on transfers of value. It mainly hits estates on death, but lifetime gifts made within seven years can be caught too.

scenes.heading: Headline rates
scenes.narration: The death rate is forty percent, cut to thirty-six percent if ten percent or more goes to charity. Lifetime chargeable transfers, such as gifts into discretionary trusts, are taxed at twenty percent.

items.label: Rate on death
items.detail: Standard rate on death estates

items.label: Charity rate
items.detail: If 10% or more is left to charity

items.label: Lifetime chargeable
items.detail: E.g. transfers into discretionary trusts

scenes.heading: Nil rate bands
scenes.narration: The nil rate band is three hundred and twenty-five thousand pounds, frozen until 2030, and spouses can pass on unused band. The residence nil rate band adds a hundred and seventy-five thousand when a home goes to direct descendants.

items.label: Nil Rate Band
items.detail: Frozen since 2009 until 2030

items.label: Transferred to spouse
items.detail: Unused band passes between spouses

items.label: Residence Nil Rate Band
items.detail: Home to direct descendants; tapered above £2m

scenes.heading: PETs vs CLTs
scenes.narration: Gifts to individuals are potentially exempt transfers, fully relieved if the donor survives seven years. Gifts to trusts are chargeable lifetime transfers, taxed at twenty percent straight away above the nil rate band.

items.label: PET: gift to individual
items.detail: Fully exempt if the donor survives 7 years

items.label: CLT: gift to trust
items.detail: Immediate charge on value above the NRB

scenes.heading: Key reliefs and exemptions
scenes.narration: Spouse and charity exemptions, Business Property Relief and Agricultural Property Relief can remove big values from the estate, while smaller exemptions cover routine gifts.

items.label: Spouse and charity
items.detail: Spouse unlimited if both UK domiciled

items.label: Business Property Relief
items.detail: Trading-business assets held 2+ years

items.label: Agricultural Relief
items.detail: Owner-occupied farms; 50% if tenanted

items.label: Gift exemptions
items.detail: Annual; also £250 small gifts, marriage, income

scenes.heading: April 2026 changes
scenes.narration: From April 2026, Business Property Relief is capped at one million pounds with fifty percent relief above, Agricultural Relief is capped too, and pension funds become taxable in the estate.

items.label: BPR capped
items.detail: Only 50% relief above the cap

items.label: APR also capped
items.detail: Farm relief limited alongside BPR

items.label: Pensions in estate
items.detail: Pension funds become taxable on death

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll work through the regime, the reliefs, planning, and the impact of the 2026 reforms.

scenes.heading: Stamp Duty Land Tax
scenes.subheading: The transaction tax on property purchases in England and Northern Ireland
scenes.narration: Stamp Duty Land Tax is charged when property is bought in England and Northern Ireland. Scotland and Wales have their own separate taxes, so always check where the property is.

scenes.heading: Standard residential bands
scenes.narration: Here are the standard residential bands after the 1 April 2025 changes. The rate climbs from nothing on the first £125,000 up to 12% on anything above £1.5 million.

items.label: Up to £125k
items.detail: No tax on the first slice

items.label: Above £925k
items.detail: 10% up to £1.5m, 12% above £1.5m

scenes.heading: Reliefs and surcharges
scenes.narration: First-time buyers pay nothing up to £300,000, but lose the relief above £500,000. Buy-to-let, second homes and company purchases attract an extra 3%, rising to 5% after the 2024 Budget, and non-residents pay 2% more.

items.label: First-time buyer relief
items.detail: 5% from £300k to £500k; lost above £500k

items.label: Additional property
items.detail: Rising to +5%, announced in the 2024 Budget

items.label: Non-resident buyers
items.detail: Individuals who are not UK-resident

scenes.heading: Residential versus non-residential
scenes.narration: Non-residential rates are lower, topping out at 5%. Mixed-use property also qualifies for them, which is why HMRC disputes these claims so heavily.

items.label: Residential
items.detail: Plus any surcharges that apply

items.label: Non-residential
items.detail: 0% to £150k, 2% to £250k, 5% above; covers mixed-use

scenes.heading: File the SDLT1 on time
scenes.narration: The SDLT1 return and the payment are both due within 14 days of completion. Miss it and there's a £100 penalty, which then escalates the longer you leave it.

items.label: Late filing penalty
items.detail: Then escalating penalties

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll work through the rates, the surcharges, the main reliefs, the mixed-use battle with HMRC, and how the SDLT1 return works in practice.

scenes.heading: CGT Reliefs: The Deep Dive
scenes.subheading: Your practitioner's cheat-sheet to the major capital gains tax reliefs
scenes.narration: Module 44 covered the self assessment capital gains pages. Now we go deeper into the reliefs themselves, because knowing which one applies can transform a client's tax bill.

scenes.heading: Business Asset Disposal Relief
scenes.narration: Business Asset Disposal Relief started at a ten percent rate, rising to fourteen percent from April 2025 and eighteen percent from April 2026, with a one million pound lifetime limit.

items.label: Original rate
items.detail: Before the increases

items.label: From April 2025
items.detail: First step up

items.label: From April 2026
items.detail: Second step up

items.label: Lifetime limit
items.detail: Per individual

scenes.heading: Other Key Reliefs
scenes.narration: Investors' Relief has its own ten million pound lifetime cap. Rollover and holdover reliefs defer gains, while the EIS and SEIS reliefs reward reinvesting in qualifying shares.

items.label: Investors' Relief
items.detail: New unquoted trading shares held 3+ years

items.label: Rollover Relief s.152
items.detail: Defer gain by reinvesting in replacement asset

items.label: Holdover Relief s.165
items.detail: Gift of business asset passes gain to recipient

items.label: EIS and SEIS
items.detail: EIS defers gain; SEIS exempts 50% reinvested

scenes.heading: Rollover Relief Reinvestment Window
scenes.narration: For rollover relief, the replacement business asset must be bought within twelve months before or thirty six months after the disposal.

items.label: Earliest purchase
items.detail: Replacement bought ahead of the sale

items.label: Disposal
items.detail: Gain arises on the business asset

items.label: Latest purchase
items.detail: Final point to reinvest

scenes.heading: Stacking Reliefs Together
scenes.narration: Reliefs can combine. A client might claim Business Asset Disposal Relief on a sale, then defer part of the gain by reinvesting in EIS shares.

items.label: Client sells business
items.detail: Claims Business Asset Disposal Relief

items.label: Reinvests a portion
items.detail: Buys qualifying EIS shares

items.label: EIS deferral applies
items.detail: Gain on that portion is deferred

scenes.heading: Conditions and Traps
scenes.narration: Every relief has conditions such as ownership period and trader status. Watch the anti-avoidance rule on phoenix patterns, holdover limits, and letting relief's shared occupancy test.

items.label: Letting relief
items.detail: Only with shared occupancy after April 2020

items.label: Holdover limits
items.detail: Trade assets only; investment assets excluded

items.label: TAAR
items.detail: Catches phoenix patterns claiming BADR

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: By the end, you'll have a working cheat-sheet for every major capital gains tax relief and the conditions that go with each one.

scenes.heading: Trusts
scenes.subheading: Trustees hold assets for beneficiaries on terms set by the settlor
scenes.narration: A trust is a legal arrangement where trustees hold assets for the benefit of beneficiaries, under terms set by the settlor. Understanding trusts matters because each type is taxed very differently.

scenes.heading: Four main types of trust
scenes.narration: There are four main types. A bare trust is transparent for tax, an interest in possession gives the income to a beneficiary as it arises, a discretionary trust leaves choices to trustees, and an accumulation trust reinvests income.

items.label: Bare trust
items.detail: Transparent: income and gains taxed on beneficiary

items.label: Interest in possession
items.detail: Beneficiary entitled to income as it arises

items.label: Discretionary trust
items.detail: Trustees decide what and when to distribute

items.label: Accumulation trust
items.detail: Income reinvested for future generations

scenes.heading: Key trust tax rates
scenes.narration: Discretionary trustees pay 45 percent income tax and 39.35 percent on dividends, with beneficiaries getting a tax credit on distribution. Trustees pay capital gains tax at 20 percent, or 24 percent on residential property.

items.label: Discretionary income tax
items.detail: Beneficiaries get a tax credit on distribution

items.label: Discretionary dividends
items.detail: Paid by trustees

items.label: Trustees' capital gains
items.detail: 24% applies to residential property

items.label: Annual exempt amount
items.detail: Half the individual amount

scenes.heading: Inheritance tax: relevant property
scenes.narration: Under the relevant property regime for inheritance tax, there's a chargeable lifetime transfer on entry, a periodic charge every ten years, and exit charges when assets leave the trust.

items.label: Entry charge
items.detail: Lifetime transfer at 20% if above the nil rate band

items.label: Periodic charge
items.detail: Charge of up to 6%

items.label: Exit charges
items.detail: When assets leave the trust

scenes.heading: Compliance and anti-avoidance
scenes.narration: Since 2022, registering on the Trust Registration Service is mandatory for most trusts. And watch for settlor-interested trusts: under anti-avoidance rules, the income is taxed on the settlor.

items.label: Trust Registration Service
items.detail: Registration mandatory for most trusts

items.label: Settlor-interested trust
items.detail: Anti-avoidance: income taxed on the settlor

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover the types of trust, how they're taxed, Trust Registration Service compliance, and planning, including trust accounts, the trustees' SA900 return and distributions.

scenes.heading: Non-Domiciled Status
scenes.subheading: Abolished from 6 April 2025, but legacy planning continues for years
scenes.narration: The non-dom regime was abolished from 6 April 2025. But clients who relied on it will need legacy planning for years to come, so you still need to understand how it worked.

scenes.heading: Before 2025: the remittance basis
scenes.narration: UK-resident but non-UK-domiciled individuals could elect the remittance basis, paying UK tax only on UK-source income and gains plus amounts brought into the UK. Longer residence meant a remittance basis charge.

items.label: Charge: 7 of last 9 years
items.detail: Annual remittance basis charge

items.label: Charge: 12 of 14 years
items.detail: Annual remittance basis charge

items.label: Deemed domiciled
items.detail: Treated as UK-domiciled for income, gains and IHT

scenes.heading: Old regime versus new FIG regime
scenes.narration: From April 2025, the Foreign Income and Gains regime replaced it. New arrivals with over ten years overseas get their foreign income and gains exempt for their first four years of UK residence.

items.label: Pre-2025 non-dom
items.detail: Remittance basis election, charge after long residence

items.label: From April 2025: FIG
items.detail: Foreign income and gains exempt for new arrivals

scenes.heading: Transition: repatriating offshore funds
scenes.narration: Existing non-doms can make a 50% rebasing election for capital assets, and use the Temporary Repatriation Facility to bring offshore funds to the UK at a reduced rate.

items.label: Repatriation rate
items.detail: Rises to 15%

scenes.heading: The inheritance tax shift
scenes.narration: Long-term residents of ten or more years now face inheritance tax on worldwide assets. That is a major hit for offshore trusts, which lose their excluded property trust protection.

items.label: Worldwide IHT exposure
items.detail: Applies to long-term UK residents

items.label: Trust protection lost
items.detail: Excluded property trust status no longer shelters

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: We'll cover the legacy regime, the transition rules, FIG election mechanics and current planning, including trust restructuring, pre-2025 asset sales, FIG elections and family relocation.

scenes.heading: HMRC Enquiries
scenes.subheading: Formal investigations into tax returns, and how to handle them for clients
scenes.narration: An HMRC enquiry is a formal investigation into a tax return, under the Taxes Management Act 1970 and the Finance Act 1998. Knowing how they work helps you protect your clients.

scenes.heading: Types of enquiry
scenes.narration: Enquiries range from an aspect enquiry into a single area, to a full enquiry of the whole return, to cross-tax enquiries spanning several regimes. Codes of Practice 8 and 9 deal with suspected fraud.

items.label: Aspect
items.detail: A single area of the return

items.label: Full
items.detail: The entire return

items.label: Cross-tax
items.detail: Multiple tax regimes

items.label: COP 8 and COP 9
items.detail: COP 8 civil fraud; COP 9 CDF, serious fraud, immunity

scenes.heading: Time limits
scenes.narration: HMRC has 12 months from filing to open an enquiry into a self assessment or company tax return, or from the later filing if amended. Discovery assessments reach back 4, 6 or 20 years depending on behaviour.

items.label: Enquiry window
items.detail: From filing; s9A TMA 1970 and FA 1998 Sch 18 para 24

scenes.heading: Schedule 36 information powers
scenes.narration: Under Schedule 36 of the Finance Act 2008, HMRC can issue formal notices for documents and information, including third-party notices to banks and agents. Some need tribunal pre-approval.

items.label: Formal notices
items.detail: For documents and information

items.label: Third-party notices
items.detail: To banks and agents

items.label: Tribunal approval
items.detail: Required in advance for some notices

scenes.heading: The enquiry process
scenes.narration: An enquiry moves from the opening letter, through information gathering and a meeting, to settlement discussions, and ends with a closure notice and assessment, or an appeal.

items.label: Opening letter
items.detail: HMRC opens the enquiry

items.label: Information gathering
items.detail: Documents and explanations

items.label: Settlement discussions
items.detail: COP 9 immunity, or penalties under Module 82

items.label: Closure or appeal
items.detail: Closure notice plus assessment, or appeal

scenes.heading: Your duties as a practitioner
scenes.narration: Throughout, you must comply with Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation, known as PCRT, and make an anti-money laundering report if you uncover tax evasion.

items.label: PCRT compliance
items.detail: Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation

items.label: AML reporting
items.detail: Required if you uncover tax evasion

scenes.heading: In this module
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover enquiry types, time limits, Schedule 36 powers, and how to handle clients through an enquiry.

scenes.heading: Penalty Regimes
scenes.subheading: How UK tax penalties work, and how disclosure and behaviour change them
scenes.narration: Welcome to Module 82. UK tax penalties fall into three broad categories: late filing, late payment, and errors or inaccuracies. Knowing them helps you protect your clients.

scenes.heading: Self Assessment Late Filing
scenes.narration: For a late Self Assessment return, there is a £100 penalty straight away, then £10 a day after three months up to £900, then 5% or £300 at six and twelve months.

items.label: Immediate penalty
items.detail: Applies as soon as the return is late

items.label: Daily penalty
items.detail: £10 per day, up to a maximum of £900

items.label: Further penalty
items.detail: 5% or £300 again

scenes.heading: Company Tax and Late Payment
scenes.narration: A late company tax return, the CT600, costs £100, then £200, then 10% and 20% of the tax at six and twelve months. Late payment brings 5% surcharges, plus interest from the due date.

items.label: CT600 late filing
items.detail: Plus 10% then 20% of tax at 6 and 12 months

items.label: Late payment
items.detail: At 30 days, 6 and 12 months, plus interest

scenes.heading: Error Penalties by Behaviour
scenes.narration: Under Finance Act 2007 Schedule 24, a genuine mistake despite reasonable care costs nothing. Careless errors reach 30%, deliberate 70%, and deliberate and concealed 100%.

items.label: Careless
items.detail: Innocent error with reasonable care: 0%

items.label: Deliberate
items.detail: Knowingly inaccurate

items.label: Deliberate and concealed
items.detail: Offshore matters can reach 200% under FA 2016

scenes.heading: Reducing and Suspending Penalties
scenes.narration: Coming forward early pays off: a careless error disclosed unprompted can have a 0% minimum, against 15% if prompted. Careless penalties can also be suspended if improvements are made within 24 months.

items.label: Unprompted disclosure
items.detail: Careless minimum, versus 15% when prompted

items.label: Behaviour assessment
items.detail: Based on records, adviser use and prior warnings

items.label: Suspension
items.detail: Careless penalties, if set improvements are made

items.label: Other regimes
items.detail: VAT default surcharge; Worldwide Disclosure Facility

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll work through the penalty matrix, how HMRC assesses behaviour, strategies to reduce penalties, and the suspension regime.

scenes.heading: Anti-Money Laundering and MLR 2017
scenes.subheading: The gateway compliance for every UK accountant and bookkeeper
scenes.narration: Anti-money laundering is the gateway compliance for every UK accountant and bookkeeper. The Money Laundering Regulations 2017 implement the EU Fourth Directive, with later Fifth Directive updates.

scenes.heading: Three lines of defence
scenes.narration: Think of three lines of defence: identify and verify clients before onboarding, keep monitoring and reviewing transactions, and report suspicions to the National Crime Agency.

items.label: Customer due diligence
items.detail: Identify and verify clients before onboarding, regs 27-28

items.label: Ongoing monitoring
items.detail: Keep reviewing clients and their transactions

items.label: Suspicious activity report
items.detail: Report knowledge or suspicion to the NCA

scenes.heading: Types of customer due diligence
scenes.narration: Due diligence comes in three types. Simplified is for low risk, while enhanced applies to politically exposed persons, high-risk countries and complex structures. You must also find the ultimate human owners with 25 percent or more.

items.label: Standard
items.detail: The usual level of checks

items.label: Simplified
items.detail: For low-risk clients

items.label: Enhanced
items.detail: PEPs, high-risk countries, complex structures

items.label: Beneficial owners
items.detail: Identify the ultimate human owners

scenes.heading: Practice obligations
scenes.narration: Every practice needs a written risk assessment, anti-money laundering policies, a Money Laundering Reporting Officer, staff training, and records kept for at least five years.

scenes.heading: Penalties and offences
scenes.narration: Practising without a supervisor such as ICAEW, ACCA, AAT, CIOT or HMRC is a criminal offence. Tipping off is an offence too, and failing to disclose can mean five years in prison, plus possible loss of your practising certificate.

items.label: Unsupervised practice
items.detail: Criminal offence under regulation 56

items.label: Tipping off
items.detail: Offence under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002

items.label: Failure to disclose
items.detail: Prison under section 330 of POCA

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover the regulations framework, how due diligence works, reporting suspicious activity, and the compliance infrastructure your practice needs.

scenes.heading: Professional Ethics
scenes.subheading: The IESBA Code, five principles and handling real dilemmas
scenes.narration: UK accountancy ethics is governed by the IESBA Code of Ethics, put into practice by bodies like ICAEW, ACCA, AAT, CIOT and CIMA. Getting this right protects your clients and your profession.

scenes.heading: The five fundamental principles
scenes.narration: Be honest and unbiased, keep your knowledge up to date and apply it diligently, and protect client information unless the law or the client allows disclosure. Above all, obey the law and never discredit the profession.

items.label: Integrity and objectivity
items.detail: Honest dealings; no bias, conflicts or undue influence

items.label: Competence and due care
items.detail: Maintain knowledge and apply it diligently

items.label: Confidentiality
items.detail: Protect client data unless legal duty or authorised

items.label: Professional behaviour
items.detail: Comply with laws; avoid discrediting the profession

scenes.heading: The conceptual framework
