scenes.narration: When something feels off, work through four steps. Identify the threat, judge how significant it is, apply safeguards, and if it still is not acceptable, decline or withdraw.

items.label: Identify threats
items.detail: Spot what could compromise a principle

items.label: Evaluate significance
items.detail: Judge how serious the threat is

items.label: Apply safeguards
items.detail: Reduce the threat to an acceptable level

items.label: Decline or withdraw
items.detail: If the threat is still not acceptable

scenes.heading: Threats versus safeguards
scenes.narration: The five threats are self-interest, self-review, advocacy, familiarity and intimidation. Safeguards work at regulatory, firm and engagement level, from training and second partner reviews to rotation.

items.label: Threats
items.detail: Self-interest, self-review, advocacy and more

items.label: Safeguards
items.detail: Regulatory, firm-level and engagement-level

scenes.heading: Common ethical dilemmas
scenes.narration: These are the situations you are most likely to face: conflicts of interest, pressure to join tax avoidance, finding client fraud, and relying too heavily on one client's fees.

items.label: Tax avoidance pressure
items.detail: Client pushes you to take part

items.label: Client fraud
items.detail: Discovering fraud at a client

scenes.heading: Tax rules and whistleblowing
scenes.narration: For tax work, specific guidance known as PCRT also applies. And if you blow the whistle, your disclosure can be protected under the 1998 Act known as PIDA.

items.label: PCRT
items.detail: Applies to tax work specifically

items.label: PIDA protected disclosure
items.detail: Legal protection for whistleblowers

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we will cover the principles, applying the conceptual framework, common dilemmas, and the disciplinary process.

scenes.heading: Engagement Letters
scenes.subheading: The contractual foundation of every accounting relationship
scenes.narration: The engagement letter is the contractual foundation of every accounting relationship, and all the professional bodies, including the ICAEW, ACCA, AAT and CIOT, require one.

scenes.heading: Risks of Having No Letter
scenes.narration: Without an engagement letter, fees are harder to recover, disputes over scope can turn bitter, and your professional indemnity insurance may not respond at all.

items.label: Fee recovery is harder
items.detail: No agreed basis to rely on when chasing fees

items.label: Scope disputes
items.detail: Disagreements over scope become acrimonious

items.label: Insurance may not respond
items.detail: Professional indemnity cover could fail

scenes.heading: Fee Mechanisms
scenes.narration: The letter sets out the fee basis and payment terms. The four common mechanisms are hourly, fixed fee, value based and retainer.

items.label: Hourly
items.detail: Charged for time spent

items.label: Fixed fee
items.detail: An agreed set price

items.label: Value-based
items.detail: Priced on the value delivered

items.label: Retainer
items.detail: An ongoing regular arrangement

scenes.heading: Limitation of Liability
scenes.narration: Under ICAEW guidance, a liability cap is typically two to three times the annual fee, or a specific amount.

items.label: Typical liability cap
items.detail: Or a specific amount, per ICAEW guidance

scenes.heading: The Engagement Lifecycle
scenes.narration: Use separate letters for audit, accounts, tax, payroll and advisory work. Review them annually, and issue a disengagement letter when the relationship ends.

items.label: Separate letters by service
items.detail: Audit, accounts, tax, payroll, advisory

items.label: Review and update
items.detail: Update for scope or fee changes

items.label: Disengagement letter
items.detail: Issued when the relationship ends

scenes.heading: What This Module Covers
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover letter structure, key clauses including tax clauses and reliance letters, fee mechanisms, liability caps and the engagement lifecycle.

scenes.heading: GDPR for Accountants
scenes.subheading: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to almost every practice
scenes.narration: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to all accountants handling personal data, and that is basically every practice. So getting this right matters for you and your clients.

scenes.heading: Controller or processor?
scenes.narration: Most practices are data controllers for client data, because they decide the purpose and means of processing. Outsourced functions like payroll bureaux are processors, acting on the controller's instructions.

items.label: Data controller
items.detail: Decides the purpose and means, e.g. most practices

items.label: Data processor
items.detail: Acts on controller's instructions, e.g. payroll bureau

scenes.heading: Six lawful bases for processing
scenes.narration: You need one of six lawful bases to process personal data, such as legal obligation for money laundering records. Special category data, like health or biometric data, also needs an extra Article 9 condition.

items.label: Legal obligation
items.detail: For example, money laundering records

items.label: Legitimate interests
items.detail: Special category data also needs an Article 9 condition

scenes.heading: Key response deadlines
scenes.narration: If a breach poses a risk to data subjects, report it to the Information Commissioner's Office within 72 hours. Subject access requests get a free response within one month, which can be extended.

items.label: Report a breach to the ICO
items.detail: Where there is a risk to data subjects

items.label: Subject access request
items.detail: Free response; the deadline is extendable

scenes.heading: ICO enforcement and penalties
scenes.narration: The Information Commissioner's Office can investigate, audit and issue monetary penalty notices. Fines can reach 4 percent of global turnover or 17.5 million pounds.

items.label: Investigations and audits
items.detail: ICO can also issue monetary penalty notices

items.label: Maximum penalty
items.detail: Up to 4% of global turnover or £17.5m

scenes.heading: What this module covers
scenes.narration: In this module we cover controllers and processors, lawful bases, data subject rights, breach response, and practice-level compliance, from ICO registration to cloud security and international transfers.

scenes.heading: Professional Indemnity Insurance
scenes.subheading: Mandatory cover for negligence, errors, breach of duty and client claims
scenes.narration: Professional indemnity insurance is the mandatory practice insurance that protects you when a client claims you got something wrong. Every UK accountancy body requires it, so let's see how it works.

scenes.heading: ICAEW minimum cover
scenes.narration: For the ICAEW, which is the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales, minimum cover is two and a half times fee income, with a floor of one and a half million pounds and a maximum of five million. ACCA uses a similar tiered structure.

items.label: Times fee income
items.detail: Minimum cover based on the practice's fees

items.label: Minimum floor
items.detail: Cover cannot fall below this

items.label: Maximum required
items.detail: Upper limit of the minimum requirement

scenes.heading: What is and isn't covered
scenes.narration: Cover applies to civil liability from your professional services, including employee dishonesty. But criminal acts, intentional dishonesty by a principal, war, terrorism, asbestos and regulatory fines are commonly excluded.

items.label: Covered
items.detail: Errors, omissions, confidentiality breach, staff dishonesty

items.label: Common exclusions
items.detail: Crime, principal's dishonesty, war, asbestos, fines

scenes.heading: Claims-made basis
scenes.narration: Cover applies when the claim is made, not when the mistake happened. That's why continuous cover is essential, including run-off cover, typically six years or more, after a practice closes.

items.label: Act or error occurs
items.detail: Not the trigger for cover

items.label: Claim is made
items.detail: Policy in force now must respond

items.label: Run-off cover
items.detail: Keeps you protected after the practice closes

scenes.heading: If a claim arises
scenes.narration: If something goes wrong, notify your insurer straight away of both circumstances and claims, never admit liability, and cooperate fully. Remember you also pay the excess on each claim.

items.label: Notify immediately
items.detail: Tell the insurer of circumstances and claims

items.label: Don't admit liability
items.detail: Leave that to the insurer

items.label: Cooperate fully
items.detail: Work with the insurer throughout

scenes.heading: Practising without PII
scenes.narration: Without this insurance you simply cannot practise, your supervisor can take disciplinary action, and you could be personally liable for clients' losses.

items.label: Cannot practise
items.detail: Cover is a condition of practising

items.label: Disciplinary action
items.detail: From your supervisory body

items.label: Personal liability
items.detail: You may bear the losses yourself

scenes.heading: In this module
scenes.narration: In this module we'll cover the requirements, what's covered, the exclusions, what drives your premium, such as fee income and claims history, and the claims process.
